Definition of done:
- Invite tokens are 32 random bytes from crypto/rand in unpadded base64url. Only the SHA-256 hash is stored, and the token appears only in the invitation email. No POST or GET response and no snapshot contains it.
- POST /v1/invites/accept returns 404 `invite_not_found`, 410 `invite_used`, or 410 `invite_expired` (more than 7 days after creation, on the service clock). Re-inviting an address (case-insensitive) revokes the old invite, so only the newest token works.
- GET /v1/invites lists only pending invites, each with `expires_at`. Tests cover each rule, and `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` all pass.

Changes:

- **`internal/store/store.go`**
  - Tokens are now 32 random bytes in unpadded base64url (`newInviteToken`), and only the hex SHA-256 is kept (`hashInviteToken`).
  - `CreateInvite` revokes pending invites for the same address (case-insensitive) before issuing the new one. Its signature is unchanged, and the returned invite carries the plaintext token.
  - `AcceptInvite` looks up by hash. It checks revoked (not found), then accepted (`ErrInviteUsed`), then expired (`ErrInviteExpired`).
  - New `PendingInvites(orgID, now)`. The existing `Invites` is unchanged.
  - New sentinel errors `ErrInviteUsed` and `ErrInviteExpired`.
- **`internal/store/types.go`**: `Invite.Token` is `json:"-"` and no longer stored. `TokenHash` is added, and `ExpiresAt()` is a new method.
- **`internal/api/team.go`**
  - Invite responses go through a new `inviteView`, which omits the token and hash and adds `expires_at`.
  - GET uses `PendingInvites`.
  - Accept maps the two new errors to 410 with the codes from the spec.
- **`internal/api/api_test.go`**: new `TestInviteTokens` and `TestInviteExpiry`. They cover token format, absence from answers and snapshots, re-invite revocation, single use, revocation, unknown tokens, exact-7-day acceptance, and expiry one second later. The existing `TestTeam` passes unchanged.

Things I did not do, which you may want to decide on:

- **Old snapshots**: a snapshot saved before this change holds plaintext tokens and no hash. Those invites will not match after a restore, so they fail closed. I did not add a migration, and the old file still contains the plaintext tokens.
- **Viewers can still list invites**: GET /v1/invites is still open to every member, so viewers see emails and roles. The task only asked to remove the tokens, so I left the access check alone.
- **Expired invites are kept**: they are not revoked or cleaned up. They are only excluded from listing and acceptance.
- **Not run**: I did not run `gofmt`, since it is not on the allowed command list. I formatted by hand to match the surrounding code.
